 Judgment
This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 27-08-2023 at about 5.00 a.m., the Petitioner was a pillion rider in a motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-EU-0977 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle) on Kunigal-Anchepalya Main Road, near Gottigere village road humps, Kunigal taluk, Tumkuru, at that time, the rider (father of petitioner) of the said motorcycle rode the same with high speed and in rash and negligent manner, lost control over the vehicle and dashed to the road humps.
Due to the impact, Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
He was immediately taken to Kunigal Govt. Hospital, wherein after first aid, he was shifted to Adichunchanagiri hospital, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and unable to lead normal life as earlier.
It is claimed that Petitioner has spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- for treatment, medicines, conveyance and other charges.
At the time of accident, Petitioner was aged 23 years, was studying in Bachelor of VOC in Product Design (6th Sem) and part time job at private company and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries, he has lost his earning capacity and income.
As the accident was caused due to negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1- Insured and Respondent No.2-Insurer.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.2 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed the written statement.
The respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court and he was placed exparte.

4. The respondent No.2 has filed its written statement and admitted the issuance of policy to the alleged offending vehicle and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
Further, denied the contents of petition averments in toto.
It has contended that the accident was caused due to the negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle and both rider and pillion rider consumed alcohol and it is a self accident.
It has contended that, the rider of offending vehicle was riding the vehicle without driving license and without helmet.

It has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner, and the future expenses claimed by him, expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that on 27-08-2023 at about 5.00 a.m. on Kunigal- Anchepalya main road, near Gottigere village road humps, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur, he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident, while he was pillion rider in motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-EU-0977, due to the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the said motorcycle?

sentences.text: The respondent no 2 has contended that PW1 was drunken at the time of alleged accident and the same has been mentioned in the MLC.
Due to his negligence he might have fell down from the two wheeler bearing registration No, KA-06-EU-0977 and sustained simple injuries.

The rider of the two wheeler bearing registration No, KA-06-EU-0977 was none other than father of the petitioner and charge sheet has been filed against the father of the two wheeler and it is collusive claim petition.
13. Keeping in view of the arguments addressed by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 once again I have perused the material available on record.
Ex.R3 mentioned that breath smell of alcohol.
No doubt the EX R3 is mentioned that at time of alleged accident the petitioner consumed alcohol.
However no documents establish that due to consumption of alcohol the petitioner has lost the control of motorcycle and fell down and thereby caused the accident.

Further, on perusal of the charge sheet, complaint and FIR, prima-facie establish that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of rider of the offending vehicle and not on the part of petitioner.
Neither the respondent No.2
has challenged the charge sheet before any authority nor rebut the evidence lead by the petitioner.
Therefore, the contention raised by the respondent No.2 holds no water.
14. By looking into the oral and documentary evidence it is clear that accident occurred due to the negligence of rider of offending vehicle.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
Therefore, this tribunal concludes that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Thereby the accident occurred and petitioner has sustained injuries in a RTA.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.2:
The respondent no 2 has taken contention that the owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and condition incorporated in the policy.

Therefore, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner and respondent No.2-insurance company is absolved from its liability to reimburse the owner of the offending vehicle.
The onus of proof will be on the person who wants to rebut the presumption.
In order to prove, the respondent no 2 not produced any documents.
The Respondent no. 2 has failed to prove its defence.
Hence I answer issue no.2 in the negative.

2. Lacerated wound on right side of head.
3. Lacerated wound on left side ear and ear pinna.

sentences.text: 23. On perusal of the record, it appears that the age of the petitioner as on date of the alleged accident was about 23 years.
The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the injured could be assessed at Rs 16,000/- Per Month.

Thus, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
24. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability: Looking into the nature of injuries, it definitely affects the working capacity of any person.

As the Petitioner is a student and also taking tuition, considering nature of injury and doctor's evidence the total functional disability of the Petitioner is considered at 5%.
25.

Further the petitioner was aged about 23 years as on date of alleged accident and the multiplier applicable to the petitioner as per decision laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 18.
The notional income taken as Rs 16,000 x 12 x 18 x 5/100= Rs1,72,800/- towards loss of future income.
26. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has sustained head injuries and was inpatient for a period of 9 days which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .25,000/- would be just and fair compensation under the head pain and sufferings.
27. Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is sure to suffer in his day today activities and face hardships.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .15,000/- under loss of amenities of life.
28. Medical expenses:

Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.14 amounting to .1,58,237/- The Respondent has not seriously disputed the medical bills.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded compensation of 1,58,237/- towards Medical Expenses.
29. Future medical expenses: PW-3 has stated that the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implants and estimated cost of surgery is Rs.40,000/-.
But he has not produced any estimation report.
In the absence of material evidence, it is just and reasonable to award Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses.
30. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:

Ex.P.11-Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at Adichunchanagiri Hospital, B.G.Nagara, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient from 27-08-2023 to 05- 09-2023 i.e, for a period of 9 days.

Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .25,000/- under the head of conveyance, food,
nourishment and attendant charges.
